details:
As we cannot use our own scripts in VRChat, we're limited by what's whitelisted for components. Which is largely built-in Unity ones for anything not very specific to and made by VRChat. The Rotation Constraint component built into Unity, along with the Translation/Scale/Parent components, operate at relative angles to what the two objects orientations are in the Unity editor regardless of what the axis of the constrained object is. Not simply taking axis movement and directly copy/pasting that amount of movement to the constrained axis.
Now, for certain behaviours, this is perfectly fine. Mandatory/preferable over direct-axis translation to the other axis even in many cases. And for those cases, how things are now is amazing, as the maths required to be able to rotate something based on the arbitrary axis of the source object instead of simply copying values to the corresponding axis is incredibly difficult. The problem is, when you DON'T want that behaviour and want to be able to just go “X axis on the first object moves X axis on the other constrained object Y amount.”
To script this as a component is dead easy (It's literally taking the change in rotation/position/scale of one object and pasting that difference to the other object) to create, hence the reason that is not a built-in component in Unity. We cannot use our own scripts though, making such things impossible in VRChat.
So my proposal is,
A new set of component types that come with the VRC-SDK called “Direct Rotation Constraint”, with Translation/Scale/Parent equivalents. Operating in a similar fashion to the existing constraints, except it makes it's changes based on the local axis of the individual objects instead of relative to the axis of the source object(s) like the existing constraints do now.
Which from an interface standpoint is nearly identical and has all the same options (So ability to set multiple objects to be sources with weights, position/rotation/scale at rest, lock axis, etc.) the Unity native one has, except with two key additional options:
> The ability to set which axis of the source object(s) affect the axis of the constrained object. For example, you want the rotation of the Y axis of the source object to change the Z axis of the constrained object instead of the Y axis of the constrained object. I imagine a interface of the three axis of the source on one side of a box with the 3 axis of the constrained object on the other, and being able to connect axis together like you would with connecting the nodes of the Udon Node script system.
> The ability to invert the effects of axis. So if a object is rotated +12 degrees on the axis that's driving the rotation constrained axis, it would rotate that constrained axis -12 degrees instead. Easiest thing would be to have that as a toggle next to the constrained axis column with the previously described node-connect method of setting which axis affects what. 
All of that was a very long winded way of describing something that should be incredibly simple if implemented, and would make previous functionally previously literally impossible now possible. For example, fingers on bat wings actually drivable by a humanoid rig as bat fingers need to be off-axis to look right. And duplicate arms being able to be off-axis from the source real arms, meaning they won't look as blatantly obvious they're constrained together. And far, far more examples I'm sure I can't even think of.
Thank you for any consideration, and I hope to see a time when avatar and world customization is extended to being able to do even more crazy things with an addition that in the grand scheme of things is incredibly simple.
title: [FEEDBACK] Constraints with Axis Driven Directly instead of only Relative
